relationships.name: Association
relationships.meaning: Two classes know about each other ("uses", "has a reference to").
relationships.draw: Plain line, optional open arrow for direction.

relationships.name: Aggregation
relationships.meaning: Whole–part where the part can exist on its own (a Team has Players).
relationships.tip: Hollow diamond on the whole. In Redpen, draw the line from part to whole.
relationships.draw: Line with a hollow diamond at the whole.

relationships.name: Composition
relationships.meaning: Whole–part where the part dies with the whole (an Order has OrderLines).
relationships.tip: Test: delete the whole. Does the part still make sense? If no, composition.
relationships.draw: Line with a filled diamond at the whole.

relationships.name: Generalization
relationships.meaning: "Is a": a subclass inherits from a superclass.
relationships.tip: Arrow points from child to parent. Works for actors too.
relationships.draw: Solid line with a hollow triangle at the parent.

relationships.name: Realization
relationships.tip: Dashed, not solid. Do not confuse with generalization.
relationships.draw: Dashed line with a hollow triangle at the interface.

relationships.name: Dependency
relationships.meaning: One class temporarily uses another (parameter, local variable).
relationships.tip: Weakest link. Use it when the other class is not stored as an attribute.
relationships.draw: Dashed line with an open arrow at the used class.

relationships.name: Include
relationships.meaning: A use case always runs another one as part of itself.
relationships.tip: Arrow from the base to the included use case. Label «include».

relationships.name: Extend
relationships.meaning: A use case optionally adds behaviour to a base use case.
relationships.tip: Arrow from the extension to the base. Label «extend». Opposite direction to include.

classKinds.name: Class
classKinds.note: Concrete type. Name in bold, attributes, then operations.

classKinds.name: Abstract class
classKinds.note: Cannot be instantiated. Name in italics or «abstract».

traps: Arrow direction: generalization and realization point at the parent / interface. Extend points at the base, include points at the included use case.
Diamonds sit on the whole, never on the part.
Dashed vs solid: realization is dashed, generalization is solid.
Actors live outside the system boundary; use cases live inside it.
Never connect two actors with an association. Use generalization if one is a kind of the other.
Many-to-many in an ER diagram needs a link entity with two foreign keys.
Read crow's foot ends at the entity they touch: the symbol next to Order says how many Orders.
Use nouns for classes and entities, verbs for use cases.

steps.title: Underline the nouns
steps.body: Candidate classes, entities or actors. Merge synonyms, drop attributes.

steps.title: Circle the verbs
steps.body: Candidate use cases or relationships between the nouns.

steps.title: Look for "is a" and "has a"
steps.body: "Is a" is generalization or realization. "Has a" is association, aggregation or composition.

steps.title: Add numbers
steps.body: Words like "many", "at least one", "optional" become multiplicity or cardinality.

steps.title: Re-read the text against your diagram
steps.body: Every sentence should be visible in the drawing.
